newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa ends off day's lows, focus on tenders.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa ends off day's lows, focus on tenders.

text.p: London cocoa futures were lower but off the five-month lows with benchmark December falling to the widely-watched 965 stg support at one stage, traders said.
But the spotlight was on tenders after some 21,250 originals or 215,200 tonnes of cocoa were posted in what some traders said was the largest in one day.

A single large long trader was believed to have received virtually all the cocoa at the start of the September delivery and market sources said he has further net long positions of 8,000 to 9,000 10-tonne lots.
This brings the trader's total position in September to around 300,000 tonnes. The previous record delivery at the London Commodity Exchange was around 250,000 tonnes in March 1995.
Benchmark Dec briefly dipped to the key support of 965 stg a tonne, the lowest since March 27, before ending at 966 stg, still a 12 stg loss.
September fell four stg to 939 stg, narrowing the September/December spread to 27 stg from Friday's 37.
Overall volume on the exchange reached 6,697 lots, with activity subdued by the holiday closure in New York.
News of the tonnage tendered on Monday was not unexpected but traders said a major concern is the major long's next move.
"The question is what he does with the cocoa. Does he put it back?" said one. "That's what no-one else can't tell."
